title: Matching to Compare
objective: Two groups can be compared by pairing them up one-to-one, without needing to count either group first.
studentQuestion: Which group has more — can you tell without counting?
newIdea: One-to-one correspondence used as a comparison tool, not just a counting tool.

teaching.setup: Two unequal small groups (e.g. 5 and 7), not yet counted.
teaching.see: Which looks like it might have more? Let's check.
teaching.break: Pair one object from each group together, one at a time.
teaching.build: Notice which group runs out of partners first.
teaching.transform: Re-pair the same two groups in a different order — same group still has leftovers.

check.prompt: Count both groups to confirm the pairing result.

examples.second: 6 vs. 6 counters (no leftovers either way — introduces equal).
examples.transfer: Two groups of classroom objects the learner selects themselves.

mastery.evidence: Uses pairing (not just counting) to correctly identify the larger of two groups at least twice.
